t: Work
d: The case studies from Best Egg, Chainlink Labs and Auth0, each with the business result.

t: Blog
d: Positions on design leadership, where product design is heading, and trust in fintech and web3.

t: How I lead
d: I set strategy clearly enough that the team can make its own calls, then spend my time on feedback and quality rather than approvals.

t: About
d: Director of Product Design II, Best Egg

t: Get in touch
d: I’m happy to walk through any of these case studies in more depth, or share the full presentation.

t: Agentic design system audit and remediation
d: Built the agent that audited Best Egg’s whole design system and directed the remediation: 86% fewer button variants, and the component picker cut 66%.

t: Cross-Sell: Vehicle Equity & Home Secured Loans
d: Turned a loan decline into a second offer instead of a dead end. A 0→1 feature across two secured products shipping on separate release cadences.

t: Verifications
d: Closed the loop after document upload: applicants can see their status instead of calling to ask. Verification rate is 71% against 61% for control in a live A/B test.

t: Refinance offers on native mobile
d: Put a refinance offer in the Best Egg app for customers who qualify for a lower rate, in place of a generic invitation to apply for another loan. Live for every customer since September 2026.

t: Staking v0.1
d: Put pool capacity, reward rate and eligibility next to the stake action, so nobody had to leave the page to decide.

t: No-code tools
d: Let teams build authentication flows through visual configuration instead of code, without taking away the control developers need.

t: Promote on decisions you wrote down
d: 67% of companies tie promotion to AI skills. Designers say they can’t fully account for their own output, so the evidence has to be recorded early.

t: A design review can’t see accessibility
d: WebAIM found WCAG failures on 95.9% of a million home pages and 56.1 errors on the average one. Those defects don’t show up in a screenshot.

t: The dispute form has no agent option
d: Agent purchases get disputed under codes written for stolen cards, and Regulation E’s own definition may defeat the box a person picks.

t: The bottleneck moved and the budget didn’t
d: Developers and engineering leaders both name reviewing AI output as their top constraint. Teams are spending the gain on deferred hires instead.

t: Disclose the review, not the tool
d: 58% of creatives have used AI on client work without saying so. The label they’re all arguing about carries a penalty and no information.

t: A name match is not a verdict
d: Europe just updated its payee name check and the UK wants to keep its own for good. A match confirms the name. Banks are printing verified.

t: Count the drift, not the adoption rate
d: Design system buy-in fell from 42% to 32% in a year. Teams are told to build a business case from a return only 5% of them measure.

t: Prototypes that cannot fail are demos
d: 43% of companies expect a working prototype as the deliverable. A deliverable gets approved. A prototype is supposed to be able to come back wrong.

t: Train juniors on what they reject
d: AI closed the output gap between junior and senior designers and hid the judgment gap. Review what juniors throw away, not just what they ship.

t: Your design system checks spelling, not judgment
d: Eighteen of 21 major design systems now ship an MCP server for agents. What they enforce is the vocabulary. The usage guidance is the part getting cut.

t: Stablecoin trust is decided at redemption
d: Congress spent the year fighting over stablecoin rewards. The OCC’s proposed rule already defines the bad day: a 10% run turns two days into seven.

t: Metered pulls make frequency a consent question
d: Banks now charge aggregators for each data pull. How often an app checks your account is about to be decided somewhere. It belongs on the consent screen.

t: Your team stopped taking your advice
d: Peer learning among designers went from 24% to 70% in a year while learning from leadership halved. That’s structural, and most leaders answer it wrong.

t: Stop hiring for AI fluency
d: Half of design leaders now weigh AI fluency in hiring, while the average toolstack went from three tools to seven in a year. That screens for recency.

t: Agent payments are a consent problem
d: Mastercard and Visa are building payment rails for AI agents. Liability follows authorization, so delegation is an interface problem first.
